title: Edge Runtime
definition: A strictly limited, incredibly fast execution environment based on Web APIs (like Service Workers) rather than full Node.js. It runs on CDN nodes globally rather than in a single centralized datacenter.
simpleExplanation: Traditional servers (Node.js) are heavy and sit in one location (like New York). Edge computing strips away all the heavy parts of Node, creating a tiny Javascript engine that is so small it can be copied to hundreds of servers around the world. The code runs physically close to the user.
realWorldExample: Next.js Middleware. If a user in London tries to access a protected page, you don't want their request traveling to a database in California just to get rejected. The Edge Runtime executes the Middleware code in a London datacenter, bouncing them instantly.

basic: Does the Next.js Edge Runtime have access to standard Node.js APIs like `fs` (File System) or `crypto`?
intermediate: Why does Next.js force Middleware to run exclusively on the Edge Runtime?

answers.question: Access to fs?
answers.answer: No! This is the biggest limitation. The Edge runtime ONLY supports standard Web APIs (like `fetch`, `Request`, `Response`). You cannot read local files or use heavy Node modules.

answers.question: Why exclusively Edge?
answers.answer: Because Middleware intercepts *every single request*. If Middleware ran on a slow, centralized Node server, it would add a massive latency bottleneck to the entire application. Edge execution is practically instant.
